title: upgrade-attention-kernels-flashattnv2-rope-fused-kv-batching
author: Ava Chan
description: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops and KV-aware batching and scheduling. This PR replaces the legacy flash_attn kernels with a new FlashAttentionV2 implementation that includes: fused rotary/rope math to avoid extra transposes, combined softmax+dropout fusion, and memory layout optimizations for KV caching. It also adapts the runtime scheduler and continuous batcher to be KV-cache aware so that repeated decode requests reuse fused KV buffers when possible. Motivation: reduce per-token latency and memory pressure for long-context decoding workloads and improve throughput for mixed sequence-length request patterns. Summary of impact: p95 latency reduced by ~20% on 8k sequence decode workloads, end-to-end throughput improved by ~1.5-1.8x for batch-heavy workloads, peak GPU memory usage reduced by ~25-35% on common LLM configs, and reduced kernel launch overhead for many small-generation requests. Implementation notes: the CUDA kernels live under runtime/attn/flashattn_v2.* and are guarded by a feature flag that falls back to the previous kernels for architectures that do not support the fused ops. The scheduler changes live under runtime/scheduler and runtime/batching and introduce a small KV buffer cache keyed by model+session to avoid repeated KV packing overhead. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains identical for existing API users; behavior is opt-in per deployment config until a staged rollout completes. Related work: builds on previous FlashAttention upgrades in pr-61234 and pr-67239 and ties into the KV caching refactor from ENG-1410.
commits: feat(attn): add FlashAttentionV2 CUDA kernels with fused rotary/softmax/dropout and improved memory layouts
perf(scheduler): make continuous batcher KV-cache aware and reuse packed KV buffers across decode requests
chore(tests): add integration perf tests and microbench harness for flashattn_v2
fix(build): add compile-time guard for older CUDA toolkits and update CI matrix
review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Nice work, big win for throughput. Two requests: add a microbenchmark that exercises many small decode calls to validate scheduler behavior and add a feature flag config param with rollout notes.

Ava Chan (reply): Added microbenchmark under tests/attn/flashattn_perf_test.py and documented the rollout flag in docs/perf/attn-kernels.md. See commit 'chore(tests): add integration perf tests and microbench harness for flashattn_v2'.
Lina Patel: There was an intermittent CI failure on Ubuntu CUDA11 when running the rope unit tests. Can you add a fallback path and a CI matrix change?

Ava Chan (reply): Added compile-time guard and fallback implementation in runtime/compat/flashattn_fallback.cpp and updated ci/workflows/flashattn_v2.yml to run on the widened matrix. The failing test was due to a CUDA intrinsic not available on older toolkits; fallback avoids that path.
Ethan Park: Please add more telemetry (histograms) around KV reuse hit/miss rates so we can evaluate rollout. Also remove a few expensive small allocations in the continuous batcher.
Ava Chan (reply): Added kv_reuse_ratio and kv_pack_time histograms to runtime/scheduler/kv_cache_manager.cpp and optimized allocations in continuous_batcher. Regression tests added.
Marco Ruiz (approval): Approving after CI green and perf numbers reproduced on perf-lab cluster.
ci_summary: CI matrix run: linux-cuda12 (unit+integration+perf) passed after second run; linux-cuda11 had intermittent rope unit test failures fixed via fallback; macOS (cpu-only) passed. Perf validation job on perf-lab/rgx-8xA100 reproduced ~1.6x throughput on target model with 8k context. Total CI runs: 4; notable failures: initial lint error and CUDA11 unit test; final status: pass.
merge_outcome: merged via squash-merge after CI green and perf validation; changelog entry added to docs/perf/attn-kernels.md; feature gated rollout enabled for Canary accounts.
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope operations, resulting in ~1.5-1.8x throughput and ~20% p95 latency reductions on long-context workloads; Memory: reduced peak GPU memory by ~25-35% for common configs; Ops: scheduler and continuous batcher now reuse packed KV buffers to lower per-token overhead; Rollout: feature-gated and canary-first deployment; Compatibility: automatic fallback for older CUDA toolchains.
notes: This PR touches low-level CUDA kernels and scheduler code; please coordinate with infra for the canary rollout and perf lab runs before broad release.
